tagline: A high pass and limestone walls on the way down.
intro: From the Buffalo side, US 16 crosses the Bighorn National Forest and crests at Powder River Pass, 9,666 feet above sea level. The pavement has two lanes. Across the range, switchbacks and hairpins work their way between the limestone walls of Ten Sleep Canyon.
The route gives a view of Cloud Peak, 13,167 feet high. Down in the canyon, rock climbers have furnished the walls with names of their own, including the less reassuring Wall of Denial.

moments.title: Powder River Pass
moments.text: Also known as Muddy Pass, the 9,666-foot crest is the high point of US 16, with Buffalo on one side and Ten Sleep on the other.

moments.title: Ten Sleep Canyon
moments.text: Switchbacks and hairpins carry the road between limestone walls, some of them named Home Alone and Plea Bargain by rock climbers.

practical: Snow can fall in any month at these elevations, though it rarely affects travel in summer and early fall.

sources.label: Wyoming Office of Tourism, Cloud Peak Skyway Scenic Byway
